items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: Joe Oliver had Bob Schauffer. And he also had Kid Ory.

ctx.x: Well, there's a couple other fellas here on the list. Joe Oliver, can you tell us what kind of a fella he was?

Fine fella. Swell guy. Full of fun. I work right opposite. Louie and I work opposite. And don't think, cause Louie and I was across the street. Joe Oliver had Bob Schauffer. And he also had Kid Ory. He had Joyce Field there, too. He had Kid Ory with him. Don't think the plantation was packed. Like our place was packed. Both in cabaret right opposite each other. It was packed. Danny had the apex across the street after hours. All the places would be packed. It was a good day. Yeah, it was a good day. Bob Schauffer…
Same Bob Schauffer. Now, Joe was full of fun. Full of fun.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: what's his name to get a trombone player? Oh, I know him. Kid O'Ree.

ctx.x: the parades away from us now? What's that? A street band?

A street band. And we had the band to do it. George Field, the Dutre. And that fellow, what's his name to get a trombone player? Oh, I know him. Kid O'Ree. And they had, oh, we had about two of us. Oh, I know him. Oh, well, he died. Well, they didn't let us put up that brass band of Louis, myself, King Oliver, and Lee Collins, and Oliver. We had a gang of us. We'd come down that street, we'd kill them. And we just needed 12 men. You know, we didn't have no big bands if we wanted, Johnny.

Mr. Dominant, really, it seems like you're about to last at the Ohegan's, aren't you? Huh? You're about to last at the Ohegan's, aren't you? Yeah. Me and Louie and I? Yeah. I found on TV the other night. Yeah. He's failing, kid. Yeah, he is.
